evidence.claim: The owner requires one backend-consumable Helm chart for the MMO application.
The current MMO registry row deliberately has no chart, runtime policy or pipeline and remains non-provisionable until those product decisions exist.
The current Academy chart and its installer tool are owned together by an external Nivo repository root rather than the backend checkout.
ChartSourceService resolves registry chart references and optional versions while refusing null, unsupported or missing filesystem chart sources before Helm runs.
The generic application registry stores exactly the chart argument and optional Helm version consumed by the installer.

The owner approved starci-lab/nivo-charts/charts/mmo as a generic chart requiring image repository, image tag and service port, with configurable ingress, persistence and probes, while MMO provisioning remains disabled.
The dedicated nivo-charts repository owns Nivo Helm artifacts under charts/<chart>, with one product instance represented by one Helm release.
The chart repository validates packages with deterministic helm lint and helm template commands.
An existing clean sibling chart establishes the repository's Helm v2 application metadata shape with explicit chart and app versions.
The implemented charts/mmo artifact is a distinct Helm v2 application chart with explicit chart and app versions.
The MMO values schema requires a non-empty image repository, non-empty image tag and service port in the valid Kubernetes port range.
The MMO Deployment renders the required image and port while exposing configurable probes, environment, resources, persistence and additional volumes.
The MMO Ingress is opt-in and requires an explicit host when enabled.
The MMO PVC is opt-in and exposes explicit access mode, storage class and requested size configuration.
